app_info.subtitle: See which devices pass checks
app_info.description:
Ask about the devices in your XFA organization: which ones pass their security checks, which need fixing, and how that changes over time. XFA is user-driven device security. It checks the security of every device when someone signs in to work apps, on company-owned, personal and contractor laptops and phones, and warns people first. People install the XFA app themselves at their first sign-in, and when a check fails they fix it themselves, with the Fix button where XFA offers one or a step by step guide. XFA also finds devices through your sign-in system (your identity provider). This connector lets the assistant read those results. It cannot change anything, and it never shows the names or emails of the people who use the devices.

What you can ask:
- Which devices do not meet our policy, and what fails on each?
- Which devices have an out of date operating system, or disk encryption off?
- What do jane@example.com's devices look like?
- How many people still have no verified device?
- Which devices are affected by a given CVE?
- How has disk encryption changed over the last 90 days?

Intended users: admins and security or IT leads of an organization that uses XFA, who want answers about their devices without opening the dashboard, for example to prepare an audit or follow up on a vulnerability. A person can only connect with their own XFA account, to an organization they have access to.

What it reads, per device: the operating system and version; if the operating system and the last-used browser are up to date (the browser's name, not its version); security check results, for example disk encryption, screen lock and firewall; if the device meets your policy; verified (checked directly by XFA, usually through the XFA app) or only discovered through your identity provider; and, on request, known vulnerabilities (CVE ids).

Limits:
- Read-only. It cannot change settings, policies or devices, and it cannot start a fix. People fix their own devices in the XFA app.
- Only the one organization you approve when you connect.
- It cannot see your XFA plan, your policy rules or your settings, for example which sign-ins are checked or which checks warn or block. Your XFA dashboard shows those.
- Device lists and counts cover devices seen in the last 30 days; trends go back up to 180 days. Discovered devices show less than verified ones, and some details depend on your plan.
- Software version and vulnerability lookups describe software in general, not your devices.

test_cases.description: Identify the organization the user is connected to.
test_cases.user_prompt: What organization am I connected to in XFA?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the name and key details of the organization the signed-in user approved.

test_cases.description: Summarize device compliance for the organization.
test_cases.user_prompt: How many of our devices are non-compliant right now?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a compliance summary with compliant vs non-compliant device counts.

test_cases.user_prompt: List our devices that were active in the last 30 days.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the organization's recently active devices with their check results.

test_cases.user_prompt: Which security policies do we have configured?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the list of policies configured for the organization.

test_cases.description: Check known vulnerabilities for a software version.
test_cases.user_prompt: Are there known CVEs for Google Chrome 120?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the CVEs XFA tracks for that software version, if any.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not attempt destructive device actions.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Delete the laptop belonging to john@example.com.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it is read-only and cannot delete or change devices.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not attempt enrollment or write actions.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Enroll a new device into our organization.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it cannot create or modify records.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for unrelated requests.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What's the weather in Brussels today?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because the request is outside its device security questions.
